title: Jade Lake Insurance — intake field docket
body:
Meeting snapshot (2025-10-31)
Attendees: Riley (Redwood), Maya (Redwood), Samir (Redwood SE), Aaron Patel (Jade Lake CTO), Priya Nair (Jade Lake infra lead), Tara Lim (product).
Purpose: quick intake call to capture security constraints, deployment preferences, and load profile for a 3-month pilot (customer-facing assistant + claim-extraction backend).

High-level summary:
- Jade Lake needs a private deployment inside their AWS account (VPC peering preferred) for PHI-ish insurance claims data. They want Redwood control plane optionality: prefer private control plane with customer-managed networking and KMS.
- Initial scope: 3 devs + 1 ops using the assistant; expected steady-state 25 reqs/min, p50 end-to-end latency target <= 350ms for text-generation endpoints. Burst tolerance to ~120 reqs/min for day-end batch processing windows.
- Data residency: primary region us-west-2; logs/audit must stay in customer account. Retention policy: 90 days for debug traces, 7 years for compliance export (exported on-demand to a secure S3 bucket).

Notes / Clarifications captured in call:
- KMS/HSM: Jade Lake requires customer KMS (AWS KMS key) for model artifacts and at-rest data encryption. They asked about HSM integration for signing; we flagged as enterprise add-on (follow-up with security specialist).
- Network: VPC peering + private endpoints. No public internet access from model nodes. They prefer static egress IP ranges for downstream APIs.
- Audit logs: Must deliver structured audit events (who/when/route/model/version/request-id) to their S3 + CloudWatch. They will run SIEM off CloudWatch and S3 exports.
- Models: start with an open Llama-style model we already verify. Jade Lake asked about quantized variants vs FP16; they prefer quantized for cost but want quality baseline tests. Schedule evals on 50 representative prompts (we to provide sample harness).
- Latency: 350ms p50 target includes network hop; Redwood runtime needs to be profiled in their environment. Suggested initial instance sizes: 2x A10G-equivalent for inference pool with autoscale thresholds.

Immediate gotchas / risks (call takeaways):
- Data egress: legal flagged any telemetry leaving the customer account. Redwood must provide a prescriptive list of telemetry and opt-out knobs.
- Model drift QA: they want a safe rollback path if hallucination/regression occurs. Tie alerts to prompt-based eval suite and add automatic fallback policy to smaller/trusted models.
- Burst behavior: day-end batch may cause cold-cache latency spikes; need warmup and caching approach. Recommended: prefix caching for common templates and scheduled keep-alive probes pre-batch.
- IAM complexity: Jade Lake uses strict SCPs; any automation must be reviewed by their security team (plan for longer onboarding cycle).

Suggested pilot architecture (sketch):
- Private Redwood deployment in customer VPC (private control plane)
- Dedicated subnet for model nodes, NAT/proxy for controlled egress with static IPs
- Customer-managed KMS for disk + model blob encryption
- Audit exporter: Redwood agent streams structured events to customer S3; CloudWatch integration option
- Canary rollout: start on 1 model variant (quantized), 40% traffic, 1 day QA, expand to 100% if no regressions

Action items / owners (short):
- Provide sample eval harness + 50 canonical prompts to Jade Lake (owner: Riley) — due 2025-11-07
- Security write-up: list of telemetry fields + opt-out switches + KMS/HSM integration notes (owner: Maya) — due 2025-11-10
- Deployment runbook draft for VPC peering + static egress (owner: Samir) — due 2025-11-12
- Provision initial infra estimate (capacity + cost) for 3-month pilot (owner: Riley + finance contact) — due 2025-11-09
- Setup follow-up technical deep-dive with Jade Lake infra (owner: Samir) — schedule week of 2025-11-17

Open questions from Jade Lake (must answer before pilot kickoff):
1) Can Redwood guarantee zero model artifacts leave their account? (we provide design but legal review needed)
2) SLA expectations for p99 tail latency under burst — what fallback behavior will Redwood run?
3) Does Redwood support customer-supplied quantization pipeline or do they require us to manage quantization?
4) How granular are audit logs (request/response vs redacted metadata)?

Prompts and eval notes (seed examples they shared):
- "Extract claimant name, policy number, incident date from attached claim text. Return JSON with keys: claimant_name, policy_no, incident_date, confidence."
- Edge case: multi-claim documents with nested sub-claims — expected behavior: split into array of claim objects. They want max 2 false negatives in a 200-sample run.

Quick troubleshooting checklist for field engs:
- If p50 spikes > 350ms: check node CPU/GPU utilization, network route for VPC peering, and cache hit rate.
- On batch night slowdowns: ensure keep-alive probes were run and pre-warmed instances available.
- If audit events missing: verify S3 write permissions and agent IAM role; check CloudWatch exporter stream.

Notes to self / conversational friction points observed:
- Aaron is hands-on but legal will be the slow gate. Emphasize documentation and consent forms.
- Priya likes concrete numbers (exact retention windows, IAM role ARNs, egress IPs). Aim to provide stubbed ARNs and CIDR lists in next doc.

Next meeting: technical deep-dive (network + KMS) — target 60–90 min. Goal: finalize runbook and confirm pilot timeline.

Reference tickets / followups to open:
- Create JIRA: JL-ONRAMP-1 (pilot intake)
- Create Confluence page: Jade Lake pilot runbook (link to be added to linked_artifacts)

End of field docket.
